subject: Sprint handshake / MAP: activation agenda & GPU lead-time checks
messages:
From: Ravi Singh <ravi@orioncloud.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-16T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sprint handshake – capacity needs and ETA checks

Thanks Kimberly — quick summary of where we are and the ask from our side:

- Goal: Production inference for conversational product (customer-facing) launched as feature flag in Q4.
- Initial throughput target: 250 peak concurrent streams, ~40M tokens/month.
- Quality requirement: p95 latency target for short-chat path < 300ms, deterministic fallbacks.
- Compliance: SOC2 + restricted-data handling; we need SOC2 artifacts and audit log retention + evidence before any Private deployment.

As the purchasing team, we need a Mutual Action Plan with clear milestones (eval → canary → SOW → hardware commit) and concrete lead times for Dedicated and Private options so we can map procurement windows to product milestones.

Specific asks:
1) Estimated lead time to get a Dedicated GPU pool (H100-capable) reserved and in our control once PO is signed.
2) If we choose Private (VPC + on-prem), high-level lead time and the earliest realistic production date.
3) Suggested pool sizing and tranche plan (minimum viable vs. full production).
4) Acceptance criteria you want us to sign off on at canary.

Can we get a draft MAP and dates this week? Attaching our internal release cadence doc in case it helps.

--
Ravi
Head of Infra, Orion Cloud
[Attachment: orion-release-cadence.pdf (1 page)]

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Ravi Singh <ravi@orioncloud.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-16T12:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sprint handshake – capacity needs and ETA checks

Ravi — thanks, this is clear and actionable. I put together a first-cut Mutual Action Plan (attached) and an activation agenda below. High level answers to your asks first, then the MAP milestones.

Quick answers:
- Dedicated pool (hosted, reserved capacity): estimated lead time after PO/signature = 6–8 weeks for H100-capable tranche (depends on region/availability). We can stage smaller A100 tranches faster (3–4 weeks) if you want immediate throughput.
- Private (VPC + customer-managed networking): 10–14 weeks typical if deploying into a cloud VPC with our Private control plane; 14–20+ weeks for on-prem hardware procurement & install (depends on datacenter approval and rack availability).
- Suggested tranches: Phase 0 (pilot): 4x A100 or equivalent q4 quantized runtimes (3–5k tokens/s sustained) — 3–4 week activation. Phase 1 (canary): 8x H100-equivalent (dedicated pool) — target 6–8 weeks. Phase 2 (scale): add 16–32 H100-equivalent nodes to reach full 250 concurrent streams.
- Canary acceptance criteria: throughput smoke test (1h sustained at 60% target QPS), p95 latency < 300ms on short-chat path, end-to-end request tracing and KV cache warmup validated, SOC2 evidence & audit logs available for redacted sessions.

Key MAP milestones (draft):
1) 2026-08-18: MAP sign-off (this doc) & confirm tranche selection.
2) 2026-08-20: PO and SOW draft issued (we'll include tranche dates, SLA guardrails, and acceptance tests).
3) 2026-08-28: Provisioning window opens for Phase 0 (pilot) — target go-live 2026-09-10.
4) 2026-09-20 to 2026-10-05: Phase 1 canary provisioning and acceptance tests (6–8 week window from PO).
5) 2026-10-10 to 2026-11-15: Phase 2 scale & production cutover (depends on tranche cadence).

Risk notes / mitigation:
- H100 availability is constrained; we recommend locking the first H100 tranche in the SOW and use A100 fallback for immediate pilot.
- For Private on-prem, lead time is dominated by hardware procurement + network approvals; early start on procurement paperwork and SOC2 evidence exchange will shorten the path.

Attachments: redwood-map-v1.xlsx (MAP draft), procurement-checklist.pdf, acceptance-matrix.csv

Next steps: please confirm which tranche you want to lock for Phase 0 and whether you prefer Hosted Dedicated or Private for Phase 1. We can run a short readiness call tomorrow.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood-map-v1.xlsx (Map draft, 3 tabs)]

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-17T09:00:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sprint handshake – capacity needs and ETA checks

Kim — quick operational notes from the runtime/infra side to fold into the MAP before we send final to Ravi: 

- Kernel / model fit: If Orion intends a 2-shot short-chat path we should recommend a quantized FP16/INT8 variant to reduce H100 pressure while keeping latency. That can shave required pool size by ~30%.
- KV cache priming: recommend a per-tenant warmup policy in Phase 0 to avoid cold-KV spikes during canary. We'll script a 48-hour warmup harness.
- Burst plan: we should offer an elastic burst to shared capacity as a cross-hold for unexpected peaks; add explicit failover in SOW (fallback to cross-region model variant).
- Supply note: vendor lead times for new H100 bare-metal are shifting; if they want guaranteed H100, include an option to convert later tranches from A100 → H100 at fixed pricing.

I'll add a short tech appendix to the MAP (est. 1 page) describing the warmup harness and acceptance perf scripts.

Ben
Director, Capacity & Onboarding
[Attachment: runtime-appendix-draft.md (stub)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Ravi Singh <ravi@orioncloud.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-17T15:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sprint handshake – capacity needs and ETA checks

Ravi / team — following up with suggested phasing details and an acceptance checklist you can sign off on. I'm pasting the condensed acceptance items here so they are easy to review: 

Phase 0 (pilot) — target 2026-09-10:
- 4-node A100 tranche provisioned in your region (hosted dedicated).
- Run acceptance harness: 60 minutes at 25% of target QPS + latency measurement.
- SOC2 artifacts: SOC2 Type II summary + log retention policy shared (redacted).

Phase 1 (canary) — target window 2026-09-20 → 2026-10-05:
- H100-capable tranche (8 nodes logical).
- Canary run: 1h sustained at 60% QPS; failover validated to fallback model.
- Observability: token-level cost dashboard and per-route p95/p99 charts enabled.

Phase 2 (scale) — post-acceptance (2026-10+):
- Scale steps documented in MAP; SLA activation on final tranche.

Financial/contract asks (ops):
- Need a Draft SOW + PO template by 2026-08-20 to start procurement.
- Add a clause for conversion of A100 → H100 tranches with 30-day notice.

If these align I will mark the MAP as approved and Kimberly — please add Ben’s runtime appendix and we can publish the final MAP. Ravi — if you want us to lock the Phase 1 H100 tranche we need confirmation by 2026-08-20 to guarantee the 6–8 week window.

Marissa Cole
Sr. Manager, Customer Onboarding
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: acceptance-matrix.csv (3 rows)]

From: Ravi Singh <ravi@orioncloud.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ops Team <ops@orioncloud.com>
Date: 2026-08-18T15:03:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Sprint handshake – capacity needs and ETA checks

Thanks everyone — this is exactly the level of detail we need. We agree to the phased approach:

- Phase 0: Lock 4x A100 pilot (please provision as hosted dedicated). Target go-live 2026-09-10.
- Phase 1: We will commit to the 8-node H100-capable tranche conditional on SOW terms; request: include the A100→H100 conversion clause. Decision to lock H100 tranche by 2026-08-20.
- Phase 2: Will be scheduled post-canary; procurement team will prepare budget after SOW.

Action items we own: PO approval and internal sign-off by 2026-08-19; start procurement paperwork now.
Action items for Redwood: Final MAP + runtime appendix + SOW draft by 2026-08-20; staging readiness call proposed 2026-08-19 10:00 PT.
